usage_notes: Official references were checked against their pages on 2026-10-18. Version-specific sources are labeled in each lesson and the current official source should be rechecked before publication. Laws, regulations, and incident reporting obligations require jurisdiction-specific legal review.

references.title: The NIST Cybersecurity Framework (CSF) 2.0
references.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
references.notes: CSF 2.0 defines outcome-oriented functions and does not prescribe one mandatory implementation. Verify the current CSF resources before publication.

references.title: NIST SP 800-61 Rev. 3: Incident Response Recommendations and Considerations for Cybersecurity Risk Management
references.notes: Final publication dated April 2025; supersedes SP 800-61 Rev. 2. Use this edition rather than older incident-response lifecycle descriptions as the primary reference.

references.title: NIST SP 800-218: Secure Software Development Framework (SSDF) Version 1.1
references.notes: Integrates secure development practices into different SDLC models; check NIST for updates and related supplements.

references.title: OWASP Top 10:2025
references.notes: The official OWASP project page identifies 2025 as the current released edition as checked on this date. Do not rely on 2021 lists as current without labeling the version.

references.title: OWASP API Security Top 10 - 2023
references.notes: Edition 2023 is the version used in this course reference list; re-check the official project for newer editions before publishing.

references.title: OWASP Web Security Testing Guide
references.notes: Use only within written scope and an isolated or explicitly authorized environment. The project page lists release information and current guidance.

references.title: OWASP Application Security Verification Standard
references.notes: Use the current published ASVS version as a verification checklist; record the exact edition used in assessments.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK Enterprise Matrix
references.notes: ATT&CK catalogs tactics and techniques from observed adversary behavior; it is not a deterministic attack timeline or proof that any one intrusion follows every stage.

references.title: CIS Critical Security Controls v8.1
references.notes: CIS v8.1 aligns control mappings with NIST CSF 2.0. Select safeguards according to context, risk, and operating constraints.

references.title: Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) Version 4.0
references.publisher: Forum of Incident Response and Security Teams (FIRST)
references.notes: CVSS is a vulnerability-severity framework, not a complete organizational risk score or a replacement for threat context and business impact.

references.title: Directions under Section 70B, Information Technology Act, 2000
references.publisher: Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In), Government of India
references.notes: The official page hosts the 28 April 2022 directions and related FAQs. This course does not provide legal advice; check scope, amendments, applicability, and current timelines with authoritative sources and qualified counsel.

references.title: Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025 and related official materials
references.publisher: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), Government of India
references.notes: The official MeitY materials index lists the 2025 Rules, corrigendum, and enforcement timeline. Applicable provisions and commencement dates can differ; verify the current official materials before acting.

references.title: NIST SP 800-207: Zero Trust Architecture
references.notes: Zero trust is an architecture approach; it is not a single product, and access decisions should be grounded in policy and context.

references.title: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5: Security and Privacy Controls for Information Systems and Organizations
references.notes: Control applicability depends on the organization, system scope, and tailoring decisions.

references.title: NICE Framework Resource Center
references.notes: Use the current NICE Framework components when mapping knowledge and skills to work roles.

references.title: RFC 9846: The Transport Layer Security (TLS) Protocol Version 1.3
references.publisher: Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF), RFC Editor
references.notes: As checked in October 2026, RFC 9846 (published July 2026) supersedes RFC 8446 for TLS 1.3. Always inspect the RFC Editor's status page for current protocol status.

references.title: Post-Quantum Cryptography Project
references.notes: Use the finalized FIPS standards and current NIST transition guidance; distinguish established standards from experimental research.

references.title: OWASP Top 10 for Large Language Model Applications
references.notes: Check the project for the current edition. Use the categories to guide risk assessment, not as a substitute for application-specific tests.

references.title: Kubernetes Security Concepts
references.notes: Provider defaults and managed-cluster behavior differ; verify the actual version and service settings.

references.title: Security best practices for Android
references.notes: Mobile application security controls are platform-specific and evolve with OS versions.

references.title: ipaddress - IPv4/IPv6 manipulation library
references.notes: The course uses this library for local calculations only; no network scanning is performed.

references.title: hashlib - Secure hashes and message digests
references.notes: Fast hashes such as SHA-256 are suitable for file-integrity examples, not for storing passwords. Use a dedicated password-hashing algorithm for credentials.

references.title: Shared Responsibility Model
references.notes: This describes AWS specifically; other cloud providers and service types have different responsibility boundaries.

references.title: Secure by Design
references.notes: Use as a design-practice reference, not as a certification or proof that a product is secure.
